1 Hero + two

Your lead pair large on top, the other two side by side underneath. Light cream, like your pages.

Good
  • The biggest, most readable thumbnail in the feed.
  • Reads as "here's my main one, and two challengers".
Weak
  • B and C come out about half the size of A, so it's not a fair contest.
  • Titles under B and C get two lines at most.

would you click?

2 Ballot grid

A 2 × 2 grid: the three thumbnails the same size, and the fourth square asks the question and carries the description and link. A dark card, so it stands out in a white Facebook feed.

Good
  • All three are equal, so it's a fair vote: "A, B or C?"
  • Big letter badges make comments easy ("B for me").
  • The question invites replies, which is what the showdown is for.
Weak
  • Each thumbnail is a little under half the post's width.

My pick: this one. The showdown is a vote, and this is the only layout that treats all three equally and asks the question.

3 Ladder

Three rows, each with the thumbnail on the left and its full title on the right, the way they sit in YouTube search results.

Good
  • Titles get room: nothing is cut off.
  • Closest to how a viewer actually meets a title and thumbnail together.
Weak
  • The thumbnails are the smallest of the three options.
  • The busiest card in the feed.

What happens when you pick

  1. Tell me which one (or a mix: "2, but with 3's full titles").
  2. It becomes a FliStudio button on a published video: it takes the in-test pairs, the description's first line and the YouTube link, and saves a 1080 × 1080 PNG next to the video.
  3. You post it to the showdown by hand.
